constitutionalNote: Seven facets, one construct (Exchangeable Entity), four nodes. The ten charter nouns are REGISTERED ROLES (classifications) over these facets — not types. This phase introduces ZERO primitives and ZERO constructs.

construct.name: Exchangeable Entity
construct.statement: An entity capable of being the subject of an entitlement, in exchange for consideration, under a governing policy, within a context.
construct.criticalField: entityRef — the exchangeable entity is ABOUT a thing; it is not the thing. One hotel room: one entity, many exchangeable entities. This prevents the classic collapse in which the product and the thing become indistinguishable and pricing becomes an attribute of the thing.

charterNounsAsFacetSignatures.note: Typical bindings used as admission rules for registered taxa — not a switch statement. A taxon's admission rule may be any registered Rule over any facets.

Offer.role: Proposal — a distinct role, not a facet binding

Bundle.structure: PART-OF composition of >= 2 exchangeable entities + one Offer over the whole

nounsNotInTheCharter.note: The platform's promise tested harder. Twelve further nouns, zero new primitives. The model is not configured to accept these; it is incapable of refusing them, because it defines none of them.
nounsNotInTheCharter.Gift card: Offer with consideration pre-paid by a third party
nounsNotInTheCharter.Loyalty point: Value with a registered unit, non-rival, periodic issuance
nounsNotInTheCharter.NFT / token: Exchangeable Entity, F6=unique, F1=digital, F4 per policy
nounsNotInTheCharter.SaaS seat: Subscription; quantitative bounds on a non-rival capability

commerceObjectModel.statement: Four nodes. Every commerce system that has ever existed is a composition over these four plus the Capability Registry.

offer.statement: A proposal, issued by an authority, to create an entitlement in an Exchangeable Entity in exchange for consideration, valid in a context.
offer.consideration: a list of Value (C-20) relationships — never a number, never a field
consequences: A price is context-dependent by construction, because Value is context-conditioned. Dynamic pricing is not a feature; it is the only behaviour the construct supports.
Multiple consideration forms are native: monetary, barter, attention, data, labour — each a Value with a different unit.
A price has an issuer and a purpose, so every price is auditable and explainable.
Currency is a unit, registered in the Unit Registry — never a hard-coded field. No Currency Lock-In is satisfied structurally.

entitlement.statement: The right created when an offer is accepted: a governed, context-bound, time-bounded permission to exercise a capability of an Exchangeable Entity.
entitlement.note: Subscriptions, licenses, memberships, and bookings ARE entitlements. They differ only in bounds and conditions — that is, in facet values, that is, in metadata.

lifecycles.note: Superseding an offer does not revoke entitlements already granted. A room does not become a different room because today it is a booking rather than a product.

cost: The platform has no opinion about commerce. It will not say what a product should cost, that a subscription must renew monthly, or that a bundle should be cheaper than its parts. Every such rule is a registered Policy owned by a commerce authority. No Industry Lock-In is possible precisely because no industry is preferred — not even the one that built the platform.
